title: Comparative kill-gate: RZ vs Interlingua vs control, precommitted criteria
description: Sol review #13 (the single highest-value next action, both reviewers agree): freeze new design; run a matched cold-use experiment — Romance-L1 readers, same narrative/dialogue/practical texts in RZ vs Interlingua vs one more control (plain Spanish or MT), measuring cloze + gist + confidence + reading time + preference, PLUS a small production arm (writers attempt a short text; time/frustration/willingness). PRECOMMIT: if RZ does not materially beat the best incumbent, stop designing a new Romance standard and redirect measurement/tooling to the incumbent. Also addresses Sol's demand-side objection (nothing measures who writes RZ text #1) and the cloze instrument's missing incumbent arms (Sol #9). title: Atlantic zonal: the English-zone auxlang (Anglo-Latinate)
description: Edward directive 2026-08-13: Romance was picked for recognizability-to-Edward, but he is EN-L1 and got gist-only (reader test 01). Design the zonal for the English zone WITHOUT overwriting RZ. Insight: the EN zone's sight-readable stratum is the Latinate vocabulary it shares with Romance — so the candidates are (a) controlled Latinate English (English grammar/spelling intact, lexicon constrained to pan-Latinate choices; EN readers pay zero, Romance readers gist it; buildable as style guide + linter + tooling) and (b) EN-weighted interlanguage (Interlingua-like with EN primary weight; small EN tax, better Romance decode). Working doc: docs/design/zonal/atlantic-zonal-v0.md. RZ continues as the Romance-zone sibling; both are recipe §8 instantiations.

title: Price the zonal auxlang against the greenfield lang (what does Romance wreck?)
description: Edward directive 2026-08-13: 'at some point soon we'll want to see what the cost of a zonal auxlang is vs the greenfield one, mostly caring about just how much it wrecks chording or script or other things i was going for, which are all of the grab-low-hanging-fruit & max-out-useful-traits variety.' Deliverable: a side-by-side pricing of the engineered traits — chorded input (one stroke per morpheme?), featural/fused script, self-segregating morphology, mode subsystems (digit pairs, dates, times), computed check, silhouette grammar, codespace discipline — asking for each: survives under a Romance-lexicon zonal lang / survives weakened / dies. Seeded by the workshop doc (docs/design/zonal/).
close_reason: Portfolio pricing shipped (docs/design/portfolio-pricing.md): full 5-column trait matrix. Direct answer: RZ keeps ONE engineered trait fully (chorded input at ~55% stroke efficiency), two weakened (script display layer, density tricks), loses the rest — buying the 0-hour receptive bootstrap for ~900M + prepaid beauty. Ceiling vs reach, not competitors. Non-obvious findings: fusion FLIPPED the script cost into a win (gap wider than when pivot was priced); capacity objection priced away (80-120 menu); modes machinery is the highest value-per-hour subsystem (ports to every column); adoption physics ranks tracks backwards from design effort. Strategy: readback card -> RZ cloze pilot -> greenfield on its own clock as ceiling product feeding traits downhill.

title: One glyph per word: fused word-blocks (~50k codepoints/char)
description: Edward directive 2026-08-09 (tentative): grow the character space toward ~50k codepoints per character — disyllabic morphemes as single fused blocks (~220x220 ≈ 48k, ~7 visual components, at the visual-crowding ceiling). Part of the four-projections vision (block glyph = 2D projection of the morpheme channel vector); see design-brief directives log.

The v0.2 stacked/headstroke layouts are interim scaffolding — the target is word-level fusion: one character per word (like a Chinese character), disyllabic fusion ≈ 48k codepoints (~7 components at the crowding ceiling), trisyllables need a fusion rule too. Elevated to P1. Design questions: component compression when fusing (which zones merge/shrink), whether POS strip + check generalize to the fused frame, crowding limits, and the beauty constraint (see beauty bead).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Fusion study v0 SHIPPED (docs/design/script-fusion-study.md, tools/fused_script.py, specimen in .ship-notes): abugida move (carrier -> attached mini-stub) + POS strip as word-level ink + stroke floor. Codespace 220^2 = 48k chars/glyph derived. HEADLINE MEASUREMENT: at equal line height, fused characters BEAT stacked blocks on worst-case one-channel-neighbor separability at every size (28px: 0.041/0.292 vs 0.000/0.159) and word length — the crowding fear was calibrated against the wrong baseline. Chording now aligns at word level (one stroke = one char = one word for disyllables). Fused is the leading layout candidate for the freeze gate. Open: trisyllable style pass (measured weak spot), AA-rendering confirmation, strip stroke weight (affects v0.2 too).

title: Capacity bottleneck ledger + relaxation menu pricing
description:
Edward directive 2026-08-09: keep careful track of the bottleneck set behind the codepoint count, and price each relaxation rung against the silent-mishearing metric (the project's ground truth, explore_noparity-style simulation).

Rungs to price: (1) cross-POS humility exemption — POS lives on the final coda, so a coda mishearing (incl. the high-confusion ∅/n) yields a wrong-class word the parse should reject; simulate whether syntactic context reliably catches POS-inconsistent mishearings; if yes, unrelated words differing only in a high-confusion coda may be exempted. (2) Disciplined context partitioning. (3) Anything else the ledger surfaces. Validate the claim that syntax exemption + context partitioning reaches ~80-120 monosyllabic root bodies without touching the phonology (current: 22 adopted / 18 strict / 18 strict_with_script / 15 after reserve). Deliverable: a ledger doc + lexgen pricing per rung, updating SPEC capacity numbers only via decided spec bumps.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Ledger established (docs/design/capacity-ledger.md) + POS-reuse rung simulated (tools/explore_posreuse.py, 400k trials): 22 -> 66 roots via POS-lane reuse costs 2.5-30 silent subs/10k words depending on syntactic catch rate q (7.4 at q=0.95; baseline 0.7). Syntax outer-code buys 20-60x reduction vs unchecked reuse. VERDICT: the 80-120 claim is validated as reachable (66 + partial domain partitioning) at a real but natural-language-sized price — a shift from engineered-rare to language-typical silent-error rates + ~2x repair burden. Product-positioning decision -> freeze gate w77. Next rungs: domain-partition sim (needs kps seed lexicon), disyllable interaction.

title: Script v0.2: anti-iconic assignment + degradation-first ink
description:
Edward directive 2026-08-09 (tentative): replace mouth-shape iconicity with anti-iconic assignment — ear-confusable phonemes get maximally distinct marks so the eye is independent redundancy; letterforms optimized for degradation, not articulatory storytelling. Keep the compositional feature grammar; reassign which phoneme gets which visual bundle, chosen against BOTH confusion matrices (phonetic pairs in channels.json confusion_policy; visual pairs in script_confusion_pairs).

Folds in the Fable v0.2 review items (.ship-notes/lang-review-conlang-657-fable.md): modifier rescale (floating bars/breaks/dot are below the small-size legibility floor — Hangul's 1446 dots lesson), strip-native full-width coda marks (POS currently rides the least legible ink while being check-invisible and lenition-prone), payload run-marking instead of per-block rings, raster-distance regression tests at 16px, gestalt-diversity/style pass (4 of 5 bases are bare strokes — picket fence). Goal state: visual confusion set becomes a subset of the phonetic one, or empty. Feed the digit implications (visual m/p = digit 4/1, n/t = 5/2, s/t = 6/2, c/j = 0/9 — digits bypass humility) into the mode-confusion model. Also deliver the stacking-vs-headstroke paragraph specimen in both layouts for the freeze gate (w77).

Reviews: Codex SHIP-WITH-FIXES (8 findings, all fixed: 4-way consistency test, phase-min floors + window guard, headstroke/dot collision, payload CLI validation, rule clearance, honest headroom prose); Fable design pass (verdict: genuine improvement, claims independently verified; ACT-NOW fixed: same-base pairs repopulated into script_confusion_pairs + priced by lexgen at 1 root body, w-cap strengthened 0.000->0.250 at 7x7). title: DECIDE: lexicon assignment policy + register architecture (human gate)
description: Three-part decision from the deconfounded exploration (docs/design/alternatives/no-parity-core.md, v2 experiment + two adversarial reviews). (1) HUMILITY ASSIGNMENT: refuse high-confusion minimal pairs among top-frequency words. Unanimous recommendation — supported in every experimental cell (deaf silent 22%->3.9%); cost 34->22 monosyllabic root bodies. (2) REGISTER: keep (A-prime: sensitive listeners get 1.4% silent + audible POS-flip flagging; costs length production for all) / drop (B: simplest; stress gets duration; sensitive lose insurance) / DEMOTE to written layer (check bit lives in glyphs + optional careful-speech realization; machine integrity kept, zero casual burden) — duke's read: demote, but genuinely open. (3) Chorded-Esperanto hybrid: hold to terms (host comparison Esperanto-vs-English, cognate-transparency scoring, exit criteria) — default remains English-host wedge. Full analysis in the two alternatives notes + .ship-notes reviews.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Freeze-gate items from the script v0.2 reviews (2026-08-09): (1) layout decision stacking-vs-headstroke — specimen now renders the same sentence in both; headstroke has NO payload marking defined (renderer raises). (2) Re-measure legibility with multi-resolution + blur-based distances before layout/style freeze — the IoU raster floor is a regression ratchet, not legibility evidence (coda n/s '1.000' is an interleaved-bands artifact). (3) Style pass candidates: j's arm asymmetry should become normative (guards +/X under handwriting slant); digit-mod-4's dark twin — every ±4 digit pair is same-base, so the system's closest visual pairs are digit pairs (0/8=c/w also check-blind); mitigations are ink-side. (4) Gestalt/beauty pass.

Sol concurs the written check needs a clearer value proposition (no independent redundancy if text stores channel vectors). (2) Freeze PREREQUISITES now explicitly include: grammar/particles (jbw), seed lexicon (kps), POS-alternation SEMANTICS (Sol: 'stone/to stone/stony is not a uniform channel operation — freezing the form before designing the semantics is backwards'), and a small complete language that can express ordinary narratives/requests/repair. (3) SSM erosion critique (Sol #3): stress-clash/destressing in frequent monosyllable strings, h-erosion, coda /s l/ instability for target L1s — needs a connected-speech stress test protocol before freeze.

title: Greenfield beauty balance: language + script aesthetics as a design goal
description: Edward directive 2026-08-13: the greenfield lang should balance beauty ('elvish, anyone?') against the other goals — and the script's beauty too. Concretely: euphony criteria for the lexicon/phonotactics (sonority, vowel harmony flavor, avoiding clinical blandness), a style/gestalt pass on the script (already flagged at the freeze gate: 4-of-5 bases are bare strokes), and an explicit statement in the brief of how much engineering-optimality we trade for aesthetic quality. Tolkien's sound-symbolism work is the reference point. Interacts with: kps (lexicon assignment), wqj follow-ons (letterforms), r5y (fused word-glyphs must be beautiful, not just distinct).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Beauty brief shipped (docs/design/beauty-brief.md) + style study (.ship-notes/beauty-study.svg): sound side — greenfield is structurally elvish-compatible (5/10 sonorant onsets, open syllables, trochaic stress); lever = kps euphony weighting (third soft preference; euphony breaks ties among adequate hooks). Script side — stroke contrast adds warmth at 0.2-0.25 but is bounded by doubled-stroke gap (scale-aware budget; trisyllables get none); standing rule: beauty lives in fonts + assignment preferences, never the feature grammar.

title: Fix worktree beads-DB confusion: hooks export 0 issues and delete tracked snapshot
description: The worktree at .claude/worktrees/modular-doodling-island has its own empty .beads embedded DB; bd auto-discovery flips between it and the main checkout DB. Symptoms: bd commands from the worktree sometimes see no issues (workaround: bd -C /Users/edward/projects/conlang), and the worktree pre-commit hook exports 0 issues, deleting the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl (had to restore + --no-verify once, commit e078ecc). Fix ideas: remove the worktree-local .beads dir or point it at the main DB via the redirect file bd supports; verify hooks then behave.

title: Zonal auxlang track: chorded Romance zonal lang first, pick zone by bootstrap mechanics
description: Edward directive 2026-08-08: separately explore an alternative to the whole channel-coded endeavor — an Esperanto-like language (a-posteriori roots, proven ~150-200h regularity wins) plus a systematic chorded input layer, targeting learning time below Esperanto's. Key tension vs current design: root familiarity is the biggest known learning-speed lever for European-language speakers but ~zero for others; channel design optimized global accessibility instead. Deliverable: design note + three-way comparison (channel-coded / no-parity variant / chorded-Esperanto) against the learning-speed target per learner population; gated recommendation.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Note revised per Fable review and landed. Two concrete follow-ups gate the hybrid decision: (a) cognate-transparency scoring over the ~2500 official Esperanto roots vs major L1s; (b) host comparison Esperanto-vs-English for the wedge. Decision folded into conlang-bf2 part 3.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward 2026-08-09: pivot from Esperanto-host to zonal auxlang. Plan: survey Romance zonal langs (Interlingua, Neolatino, Latino sine flexione) + zone-comparison criteria (receptive intelligibility, community, corpus, orthography regularity for chording, bootstrap mechanics); Romance first; keep the eventual cross-zone pick open (e.g. Interslavic's traction is a benchmark). Chording layer design follows base-language choice.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward 2026-08-09 directives: (1) program shape = replicable per-zone METHOD ('generate for the next zone if it works') — document the recipe, do NOT build a generator or manage that complexity; (2) tentatively use the WIDE chorded script for the zonal lang — FLAG: this tensions with the survey's core bootstrap finding (receptive-first langs win by meeting readers in their own orthography; Interslavic's lesson). Proposed resolution to put before Edward: standard Latin orthography as the primary/receptive surface, wide chorded script as the input method + optional dense written layer — chording wins retained, receptive bootstrap intact. Surface learning-time cost if the script is made primary.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Script-primacy trade priced: docs/design/alternatives/zonal-script-pricing.md. Verdict: Latin-primary for the zonal lang (featural-primary would cost the entire receptive bootstrap — 84%->0 first-contact — for benefits that survive as layers); wide chorded script ships as input method + optional dense display + enthusiast tier. Featural-primary remains right for the channel language.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward 2026-08-09: Romance confirmed as the proof-of-concept zone specifically so he can test receptive reading himself — first evaluation is Edward reading zonal text cold. Design the PoC deliverable as readable sample texts early (not just spec).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Workshop pass (Edward-directed, 2026-08-13): docs/design/zonal/romance-zonal-v0.md — full working design: ES/PT/IT/FR/RO weighted sources; cognate-first shallow orthography (kept 'centro', rejected LFN-style respelling); Interlingua-grade morphology with two deliberate departures (adjective NUMBER agreement — invariant adjectives are the loudest broken-Spanish signal; exactly 3 irregular verbs es/va/sta); lexicon recipe with mandatory false-friend screen (self-audit caught loco='place' reading as ES 'crazy'); THREE sample registers ready for Edward's cold-read test with a marked-blocker protocol; bootstrap plan (cloze test first, publish the number); the 8-step per-zone recipe abstracted for the Sanskritic replication. Next: 40-item cloze instrument + 2k-root lexicon with derivation families.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Workshop continuation: rz-chording.md (chord theory — onset-cluster left bank, 4-key coda bank thanks to Romance's l/n/r/s coda collapse, zero-exception chord->text mapping, honest rates: ~100-130 wpm brief-free vs greenfield's ~1.8x ceiling) + cloze-test-v0.md (26-item instrument with key and protocol, ready for a friends-and-family pilot) + §10 middle-ground analysis (no Romance-skinned greenfield; but greenfield loots cognate tables as free mnemonic-hook heuristic -> noted on kps).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Reader test 01 ingested (Edward, out-of-zone EN-L1: gist-yes/specifics-no; 18 marks classified in reader-test-01.md). Actions: cerca->proxime applied; alora flagged vs entonce; EN-Latinate tie-break added to recipe; gist/specifics dual scoring in cloze instrument. Then core-conversational.md: ~55-concept recipe pass at scale on the weakest register — false-friend screen fired twice more (vider/FR-vider, cercar/circa), EN tie-break resolved ~8 entries, ~12 FLAG rows are the cloze oversample targets. Spelling: anno adopted.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Zone pivot (Edward 2026-08-13): RZ stays (not erased), but the active zonal is now the ENGLISH zone — see atlantic-zonal-v0.md and the new AZ bead. Key analysis: pan-Germanic is wrong for EN-L1 (English can't sight-read Germanic); the EN zone's asset is the Latinate stratum shared with Romance -> two products: AZ-a controlled Latinate English (EN cost zero, Romance gist; buildable as linter+wordlist) and AZ-b EN-weighted interlanguage (parked pending AZ-a's Romance numbers). One cloze program tests RZ and AZ-a on both populations: four numbers, one experiment.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: RZ 'whole thing' pass: rz-grammar.md (complete reference — pronouns/clitics, es-vs-sta codified, negation w/ concord, questions, clauses, full numerals, derivation table, calendar; 3 irregular verbs held), rz-lexicon.md (~350 total entries field-organized; screen caught 6 more false friends: corte/rose/la/oficina/riso/large; finding: Ibero-weight strains in body/kinship/household fields), rz-texts.md (reader pack: 190-word narrative + market dialogue exercising everything; self-audit caught & fixed 7 rule violations in my own prose — the language is now hard enough to be usable and wrong in, which is progress). Next: cloze pilot on Romance-L1 readers.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: rz-script-adaptation.md: RZ channel analysis (syllable-level = codespace only; the REAL channels are the regularized suffixes — tense/number/POS, deterministic by design) + featural script adaptation (wide model: ~12 bases + voicing modifier with distance-2 doctrine relaxed for the secondary layer; carrier transfers verbatim; cluster composition mirrors chord banks; suffix logograms in the strip recover silhouette grammar in Latin-primary RZ). No renderer work until after the cloze pilot.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: RZ script TAPED OUT: tools/rz_script.py — 18 distinct letterforms (voicing ground-bar, greenfield transfer for shared phonemes), diphthong twin carriers, 4-coda strip + marginal-coda fallback, cluster satellites, suffix LOGOGRAMS (-mente/-cion/-itate/-abile; -itate redesigned to dodge the female-symbol collision). Full reader pack renders (234/234 words). Density: nacion/veritate = 2 glyph-units; suffix channel gets dedicated ink as designed. Specimen: .ship-notes/rz-specimen.svg.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Density/spacing/chording answered + implemented (rz-density-chording.md): function-word logograms (top 15, quarter-width) + proportional blocks + headstroke-no-spaces = measured 29% line-length reduction on the fable clause (2512u -> 1788u). Spacing: necessary in v0 (no SSM) but replaced by headstroke rule-breaks at near-zero cost — the layout greenfield rejected became RZ's spacing solution. Chording: NO channel rearrangement (banks = zones = phonology factorization); logograms chord as single principled briefs, so stroke count = glyph-unit count = morphological unit count.

title: Governance: versioned spec process, frozen core / open periphery
description: Context: own the spec — semver-style releases, breaking-change policy (Toaq model), dictionary proposal process, registers as formal objects (casual/careful/safety-critical). Prevents Esperanto drift / Lojban committee churn / Ithkuil completeness death.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward 2026-08-08: drift governance is in scope — versioned lexicon releases absorb frequency drift and coinage against the SPEC §8 reserved headroom. Also record: occasional Fable review for language-design milestones (CLAUDE.md review-policy addendum).

title: Seed lexicon: Zipf-assigned roots + first sample texts
description: Context: assign monosyllable inventory by corpus frequency (Zipf policy from day one); draft first few hundred roots; produce sample sentences/parallel text demonstrating SSM, POS channel, modes. Phonaesthetics deferred — placeholder forms acceptable, name still TBD.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward 2026-08-08: reserve space for new words / drift — SPEC §8 now mandates ≥30% of each POS class's monosyllable slots stay unassigned at every release; keep disyllable spacing slack. Lexicon assignment must respect the reserve.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Free heuristic from the zonal workshop (romance-zonal-v0.md §10): root-body assignment is arbitrary within confusion constraints, so prefer bodies that phonetically evoke widespread international/Romance forms for the meaning (so=sun/sol, ma=hand/mano, no=negation). Zero structural cost, measurable acquisition gain for the Romance+international cohort, serves the beauty directive too. Loot the zonal cognate tables when assigning.

title: Derivation morphology, correlative grids, particle inventory
description: Context: Esperanto-style systematic derivation (closed core ~1500 roots + productive combination); correlative-grid mechanism for ALL closed paradigms (pronouns, tense-aspect, deixis — channels = semantic axes); design particle inventory FIRST (shortest syllables are grammar's real estate); spoken punctuation/terminators a la Lojban; evidentials/attitudinals later (Tier 3).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Pre-freeze obligation (review finding 7): enumerate the full structural particle inventory (mode markers, clause openers/terminators, case/topic, conjunctions) against the 20-slot budget WITH confusion constraints applied, before the core freeze decision. Also: decide whether cross-POS root-family sharing is obligatory (spec default: yes).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Fable review addition: weigh whether high-frequency modifiers should prefer disyllabic forms (coda-s lenition flips modifier->noun, NP-internally syntax-blind — SPEC §6 honest-costs paragraph).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Particle budget update from bcq: modes consume 8 of 20 h-slots (hu number, ho date, hi time, he spell, hen phonetic-reserved, hin coord, has close, hos checksum-close — all PROVISIONAL, movable to coda-bearing slots if grammar needs the open ones). 12 slots remain for grammar. Enumerate structural particles against this before freeze (w77).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Elevated by both milestone reviews: the greenfield 'is not yet a language' — grammar, argument structure, clause combining, reference, derivational semantics (especially the POS-alternation semantics: what DOES a root's noun/verb/modifier alternation mean?), discourse conventions. This bead is now the greenfield critical path, ahead of any further script/input work.

title: Font pipeline (four-projections deliverable)
description: Deliverable from the 2026-08-09 four-projections vision (see design-brief): a real font pipeline for the block script (likely feature-data -> glyph outlines -> OTF, with the check slot as a computed layer). Explicitly LOWER priority than straightening out the script itself (Edward, 2026-08-09) — blocked conceptually on script v0.2 ink decisions.

title: Zonal: Sanskritic Interlingua (Indo-Aryan zone)
description: Edward 2026-08-09: a Sanskritic Interlingua alongside the Romance zonal lang — pan-Indo-Aryan zonal auxlang built on the shared Sanskrit-derived (tatsama) core across Hindi/Urdu/Bengali/Marathi/Punjabi/Nepali etc. Lower priority; becomes the second application of the per-zone method once the Romance recipe exists. Open questions: script strategy (Devanagari vs Latin vs multi-script like Interslavic's dual-script approach), Persian/Arabic-derived vocabulary handling for Urdu reach, and whether measured receptive intelligibility can be collected cheaply.

title: Standing: explore alternative paths to the whole endeavor
description: Edward directive 2026-08-08: freedom to explore alternatives at any level as the build proceeds — e.g. different error-correction architectures (explicit check syllables vs register bits), script-first vs speech-first framings, the spatial/argument-graph sentence layer (currently the designated sequel), non-CV templates, sign/gesture serializations, or reframing the deliverable entirely. Process: investigate during natural pauses; write findings into paper discussion/alternatives sections; substantive proposals become beads + human gate if they change project shape. This bead stays open as the mandate's home.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Edward directive: explore 'natural-grade emergent redundancy' core — no parity register, no mandatory concord; just phonotactics + SSM templates + not min-maxing word length. Investigating with quantitative comparison vs the check-bit architecture. Deliverable: design note + simulation + gated recommendation.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: v2 exploration complete and landed (970f431): deconfounded experiment with morphology; v1 drop-register recommendation withdrawn; three-way decision packet at conlang-bf2. Bead stays open as the standing mandate.

title: Input methods: chorded keyboard + phone/touch text input
description: Context: chord = glyph = sound (one channel vector, three renderings). Desktop chorded layout derives mechanically from frozen core. PHONE TEXT INPUT is first-class per Edward (2026-08-08): design touch entry — e.g. per-channel swipe/tap zones or chord-on-glass — as an adoption wedge usable inside English (numbers/dates modes standalone).

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Headroom obligation (SPEC §9, Edward directive): chord + phone/touch layouts must scale to the wide-model counts without redesign.

comments.author: claude-conlang-duke
comments.text: Four-projections vision (Edward 2026-08-09, design-brief directives log): chords = the motor projection — mirrored hands, one syllable per hand, one stroke per morpheme; skeleton input = the lossy projection — channel-subset briefs (onsets-first) resolved by IME against the dictionary, no per-word memorization ever. Priced ceiling: ~1-3k chord inventory saturates composition at ~39 bits/s, so the chording layer is optimal — density buys compactness/skimming, never WPM. IME + chord engine are deliverables of this bead; run alongside and LOWER priority than straightening out the script itself.

title: Tier-4 parking lot: phonaesthetics + true name, degraded modes, shorthand, accessibility serializations
description: Context: name decision explicitly deferred by Edward. Phonaesthetics pass happens when naming real words. Degraded modes (whistled/drummed), Gregg-style cursive projection, Blissymbolics-style accessibility serializations all derive from the frozen architecture. Spatial sentence layer is a SEPARATE sequel project — do not fold in here.

title: Tier-3 backlog: outer code + register profiles, semantic-classifier zone, evidentials/attitudinals/spoken punctuation
description: Context: build after a working language exists. Cross-syllable outer code min-max matters for the safety-critical register; semantic-classifier zone is written-only and retrofittable; evidentials/attitudinals/punctuation are ordinary grammar design.
